_about: S7 (WS6) hand-adjudication of scripts/artifact_survivorship.py's ephemeral lists. Author judgment, kept as a published INPUT (the qualitative-ratings.json / probes/scores.json / survival-audit.json pattern). data/artifact-survivorship.json is NOT edited and artifact_survivorship.py is NOT re-run: per METHODS rule 2 a re-run must never silently overwrite or invent a judgment call, and per rule 8 the published measurement stands with its correction stated beside it rather than being retroactively patched.
_provoked_by: ASSESSMENT section 5.1 lists the survivorship finding in the ROBUST half with the note 'individual names are spot-checkable'. S7 spot-checked them. Sixteen of btest's twenty-six path-attributed names did not survive.
_reader: one reader, once - no second rater, as with WS3's altitude labels and WS5's audit. Every adjudication below is individually checkable from the receipt given.

direction_of_the_bias.statement: Every false-positive class INFLATES an ephemeral count. blive's count is 0 and cannot be inflated. The instrument's noise is therefore one-directional and runs WITH the hypothesis.
direction_of_the_bias.channel_asymmetry: The auto-memory false-positive class can only reach a project whose Claude Code transcripts survived retention (channel C). Transcript files enumerated 2026-07-26: btest 10, shared-substrate 3, datacli 2, blive 0, b-autobot 0, seamQ 0, lab 0. All six btest auto-memory files that were counted carry mtimes 2026-07-11..2026-07-25 - exactly the surviving window - while the eight btest memory files with March/April mtimes are absent from the list. blive has ten memory .md files of its own (incl. feedback_warmup_discipline.md, feedback_surface_full_option_space.md, feedback_work_on_main.md); the instrument was structurally incapable of observing any of them. The headline pair was in part comparing a project whose agent-side artefacts were visible against one whose were not.

corrected_counts._note: Denominators move too: reclassified-as-committed names stay in `observed`; not-an-artefact names leave it.

headline_restatement.what_is_unchanged: The finding is narrowed, not withdrawn. Its primary evidence is the operator's own disclosure (S6) that he routinely created working artefacts and did not commit them, often deleting them; the count was always published as a lower bound; and blive's zero is independently verified against blive's git.
headline_restatement.what_must_change_downstream: ASSESSMENT section 2.6's phrase 'the strongest single number in the corpus' no longer holds, and section 5.1's robust-table row for it must carry the corrected number and the channel asymmetry.

btest_adjudication._scope: the 26 path-attributed names only. The 13 session-attributed-only names were already excluded from the defensible number in S6 (WS0-bis finding 2) and are not re-adjudicated here.

class_A_auto_memory_files.reason: Claude Code auto-memory files. They are durable on disk under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ - the opposite of evaporation - and are agent state rather than a deposit to the project substrate. artifact_survivorship.py:113 states this intent in its own comment ('memory.md and the auto-memory files are agent state, not deposits'), but NON_SUBSTRATE excludes only the literal basename 'memory.md' (the index), so the individual files pass the filter. Stated intent and implementation disagree; the implementation is the bug.

class_A_auto_memory_files.corroborating_check: The eight btest memory files with March/April mtimes (feedback_smim_approach, project_harp_paper, project_smim_known_issues, project_smim_status, project_smim_test_infra, reference_arxiv_endorsers, user_profile, plus MEMORY.md which NON_SUBSTRATE does catch) are absent from the ephemeral list. Only files written inside the surviving-transcript window were observed at all, which is the mechanism, demonstrated.

class_B_flattened_duplicates_of_committe.verdict: FALSE POSITIVE - the file IS committed
class_B_flattened_duplicates_of_committe.reason: Path separators mangled into underscores, so the basename never matched the committed pool. Each corresponds to a real docs/smim/*.md file. Verified committed in btest by `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- docs/smim/<F>.md` (exactly one adding commit each) AND present in the smim repo after extraction.
class_B_flattened_duplicates_of_committe.effect_on_denominator: These five move from `ephemeral` to `committed`; they remain in `observed`.

class_C_basenames_spliced_out_of_a_binar.reason: Adjacent strings joined by regex over JetBrains LocalHistory `changes.storageData`, which is a binary record store with no separators between path strings. is_plausible_basename() bounds length and token count but cannot detect a splice. This is the same class as the two regex defects S6 caught by hand-reading its first output (WS0-bis hand-verification); these four survived that pass.
class_C_basenames_spliced_out_of_a_binar.note_on_the_fourth: It ends in 'readme.md', which NON_SUBSTRATE would have excluded had basename() resolved it - the string contains no '/' so the whole splice became the basename.

recommended_fixes_for_any_future_run: Exclude any path under a Claude Code projects/*/memory/ directory from channel C, matching the comment already at artifact_survivorship.py:113 - not just the literal basename 'memory.md'.
Normalise separators before taking a basename, or reject basenames containing a token that also names a committed directory (this alone kills class B).
Reject basenames containing a repeated leading token (fredfred, globalglobal, reportsreports) or any non-ASCII byte - a cheap splice detector for class C.
Exclude vendored and build-output trees using corpus_common's existing vendored-path classification, which git_miner already applies and this script does not.
Publish, alongside every per-project count, the number of surviving Claude Code transcript files for that project, so a reader can see which projects channel C could reach at all.
